origin.description: zoo's as.Date generic. Plain numbers use the numeric method, which defaults the origin.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object. A number that is not an S3 object uses as.Date.numeric. A ts uses as.Date.ts.
Passed to the method. For numbers, the first argument is origin when origin is not named.

origin.details: If x is not an object and is numeric, the numeric method runs, so as.Date(0) is 1970-01-01. Everything else uses UseMethod. A character string is base as.Date. A ts of frequency 1, 4, or 12 becomes the first of the corresponding month.
origin.value: A Date vector, in days since 1970-01-01.
origin.example:
cat(as.character(as.Date(0)), "\n", sep = "")
cat(paste(as.character(as.Date(ts(1:4, start = 2000, frequency = 4))), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: zoo's as.Date generic. Plain numbers use the numeric method, which defaults the origin.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A number, a sequence of numbers, a date string, an RDate, a Ts, or a factor.

arguments.name: origin
arguments.text: Used by the numeric method. The default is 1970-01-01.

arguments.name: offset
arguments.text: Added to a ts time before the dates are built.

arguments.name: format
arguments.text: strptime pieces %Y, %y, %m, and %d, forwarded when a numeric origin is itself a string.

translation.details: Numbers and numeric arrays, including an integer array, use as_date_numeric. A Ts uses as_date_ts. A string uses the ISO date parser, or format when it is set. A factor is converted through its labels. Yearmon and yearqtr are left to their own methods. A logical value raises the base message that x cannot be converted to Date.
translation.example:
from zoo.as_date import as_date, format_dates
from zoo.as_zoo import Ts
import numpy as np
print(format_dates(as_date(0))[0])
print(" ".join(format_dates(as_date(Ts(np.arange(1, 5), start=2000, frequency=4)))))
